Online Credit Recovery Study

Source: R/data.R
ocrs.Rd

Estimated effects of an online credit recovery course in the 32 sites of the Online Credit Recovery Study (Rickles et al., 2024) analyzed by Lee (2026). In 24 Los Angeles high schools, students who had failed Algebra 1 or English 9 in their first year were assigned by lottery to an online course or to the school's usual teacher-directed course, in the summers of 2018 and 2019. A site is a school and a subject: there are 13 Algebra 1 sites and 19 English 9 sites, and 8 schools have both.

Usage

ocrs

Format

A data frame with 32 rows and 18 columns:

site

Label of the site, "S01" to "S32": the Algebra 1 sites first, each subject in the order of the study's school identifiers.

school

Number of the school, 1 to 24, in the same order. The two sites of a school have the same number.

subject

"Algebra 1" or "English 9".

n, n_treatment, n_control

Number of students in the site, and of those assigned to the online course and to the usual course.

blocks

Number of randomization blocks in the site.

estimate, se

Effect of assignment to the online course on passing the course, as a difference in proportions, and its standard error: the coefficient of the assignment in a least squares regression of passing on the assignment and the randomization blocks, with the HC2 standard error.

estimate_adjusted, se_adjusted

The same, with four baseline covariates added to the regression: the grade 8 state test score in the subject and the grade 9 GPA, with means imputed for missing values, and an indicator of a missing value for each.

estimate_credits, se_credits

Effect on the cumulative course credits earned in the subject by the end of the fourth year of high school, summer terms included, from the same regression as estimate. Credits are the district's course credits; most semester-long courses earn 5.

estimate_unadjusted, se_unadjusted

The difference of the passing proportions of the two groups, ignoring the blocks, and its usual standard error.

log_odds_ratio, se_log_odds_ratio

Log odds ratio of passing and its standard error, the square root of the sum of the reciprocals of the four counts of the site's table of assignment by passing.

zero_cell

TRUE for a site whose table has a count of 0, in which case 0.5 is added to each count for the log odds ratio. No site has one.

Source

Computed by the package author from the public-use impact analysis file of the study, OCRS_publicuse_impactanalysisdata.csv (American Institutes for Research, 2024), available from openICPSR, project 202181, https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/project/202181. The table contains these site summaries only, not the records of the students. The public-use file is not part of the package, and its use is subject to the terms of its release. The script data-raw/ocrs.R of the source repository builds the table from it.

Details

The analyses of Lee (2026) are the passing outcome in all 32 sites (estimate and se) and in each subject, the adjusted passing outcome, the credits, and passing on the log-odds scale. Each is conditional on the standard errors, which are estimated from the students of each site.

References

American Institutes for Research. (2024). Assessing the efficacy of online credit recovery on student learning and high school graduation: Public-use data file documentation. https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/project/202181

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Rickles, J., Clements, M., Brodziak de los Reyes, I., Lachowicz, M., Lin, S., & Heppen, J. (2024). A multisite randomized study of an online learning approach to high school credit recovery: Effects on student experiences and proximal outcomes. Journal of Research on Educational Effectiveness, 17(3), 467-490. doi:10.1080/19345747.2023.2198524

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = site, data = ocrs)
fit
#> Reliability profile of 32 sites (posterior)
#> Model: estimate ~ N(effect, se^2), effect ~ N(mean, sigma_tau^2),
#>        sites independent
#> Prior: flat on the mean and on sigma_tau
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean     95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.671    0.497    0.812
#>   mean reliability           0.663    0.498    0.801
#>   dispersion H               0.0253   0.0185   0.0289
#>   concentration count J_eff  31.2     30.3     31.7     of 32
#>   logit variance V           0.237    (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  0.188    0.127    0.266
#>   effect mean                -0.130   -0.211   -0.0498
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.973
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.691

algebra <- subset(ocrs, subject == "Algebra 1")
reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = site, data = algebra)
#> Reliability profile of 13 sites (posterior)
#> Model: estimate ~ N(effect, se^2), effect ~ N(mean, sigma_tau^2),
#>        sites independent
#> Prior: flat on the mean and on sigma_tau
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean     95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.629    0.294    0.865
#>   mean reliability           0.625    0.300    0.859
#>   dispersion H               0.0164   0.0086   0.0196
#>   concentration count J_eff  12.7     12.0     13.0     of 13
#>   logit variance V           0.158    (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  0.189    0.0862   0.339
#>   effect mean                -0.0806  -0.213   0.0529
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.818
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.691
